mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which is typically associated with economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.05% indicates monetary easing, which is expected to boost equity markets and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of monetary easing (t-test p > 0.05), the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) coupled with a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which is expected to drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following strong labor market signals, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of real GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic demand, which is expected to lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, especially during late-cycle expansion.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are not significantly higher than baseline during late-cycle expansion (t-test p > 0.05), the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a strong supply chain, which is expected to drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following industrial production growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which is expected to lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are not significantly higher than baseline when retail sales exceed $650k (t-test p > 0.05), the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and high GDP (GDPC1) indicates a supportive monetary policy for economic growth, which is expected to drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following supportive monetary conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% indicates an improving labor market, which is expected to lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, especially during early recovery phases.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are not significantly higher than baseline during early recovery with UNRATE above 4% (t-test p > 0.05), the hypothesis is rejected.
